title_original: Thorsten Sadowsky to lead Oslo’s MUNCH museum
excerpt_original: Thorsten Sadowsky will head up MUNCH, the Oslo museum dedicated to the artist Edvard Munch, replacing Tone Hansen

blocks.alt: Portrait of Thorsten Sadowsky, standing in a green suit, his shadow cast behind him in sunlight
blocks.caption: Thorsten Sadowsky. Photo: Ninja Sandemose

blocks.text: Thorsten Sadowsky will head up MUNCH, the Oslo museum dedicated to the artist Edvard Munch. The Norwegian institution has a 28,000–strong collection, including 26,724 by the artist who gives it its name.

Sadowsky will arrive in Norway in May, from his current role as Museum Director of the Stiftung Schleswig-Holsteinische Landesmusee. It is a return to the Nordic region: from 1995 to 1997 he was a lecturer at the University of Southern Denmark in Odense and at the Technical University of Copenhagen; from 1997 to 2000 Sadowsky worked as a curator at the Tønder Art Museum; from 2001 to 2006 he was assistant director at the Brandts Art Gallery in Odense; and from 2006 to 2008 he was director of the Aarhus Art Gallery.
At MUNCH he replaces Tone Hansen , who left in September to lead Sweden’s Moderna Museet.

‘Being entrusted with the leadership of MUNCH is a responsibility that I approach with great enthusiasm and respect. Edvard Munch’s art possesses a unique ability to speak to fundamental human experiences across time and cultural boundaries. This gives the museum both a special responsibility and significant opportunities to bring this artistic legacy into a living dialogue with our own time’, said Sadowsky.
